subtitle: Threat intelligence, vulnerability research & defensive tradecraft for security professionals
footer_tagline: Curated for cybersecurity practitioners who ship detections, not decks.
audience: Cybersecurity practitioners — SOC analysts, incident responders, red teamers, detection engineers, and security architects — who live in terminals and ticket queues. They already understand attacker TTPs, CVE scoring, and the MITRE ATT&CK framework. They need a brief that surfaces actionable threat intelligence, newly weaponized vulnerabilities, and tooling shifts before their Monday standup — not vendor marketing dressed as news.
in_scope: Active exploitation of CVEs and zero-days in the wild
Threat actor campaigns, TTPs, and attribution updates
Detection engineering: new rules, sigma/YARA releases, log-source changes
Offensive tooling releases and red-team technique evolution
Incident response case studies and post-mortems
Ransomware group activity, leak-site intelligence, and extortion trends
Critical infrastructure and OT/ICS threat developments
out_scope: Generic 'cybersecurity awareness' tips aimed at end users
Vendor product launches and feature announcements without technical depth
Compliance and audit checklists (SOC 2, ISO 27001 checkbox content)
Executive/CISO boardroom narrative and risk-appetite framing
Consumer privacy and data-broker stories with no practitioner angle
relevance_gate: Would a SOC analyst or incident responder change their detection rules, patch priority, or hunt hypothesis after reading this?

tracks.name: Threat Intel

tone: Direct, analyst-to-analyst — technical precision over narrative polish, zero vendor hype, and always leading with what defenders should do next.
